author: Great Lakes Wire
title: Bishop Walsh announces clergy and leadership appointments in Diocese of Gaylord
text:
Bishop Jeffrey J. Walsh of the Diocese of Gaylord announced on April 22 a series of new clergy assignments and leadership changes, with most taking effect July 1, 2026.
The appointments affect both diocesan leadership roles and parish positions across the diocese, which serves about 45,000 Catholics in northern Michigan. The changes are part of ongoing efforts to address pastoral needs within the community, according to the diocese.
Among the key leadership changes, Reverend James P. Hayden will retire from his position as Vicar General and Moderator of the Curia. Reverend Charles G. Donajkowski will become Vicar General after serving as Pastor at St. Casimir Parish in Posen and St. Dominic Parish in Metz, as well as Regional Vicar for the East Region. Reverend Matthew A. Furgiuele is appointed Judicial Vicar while continuing his role as Pastor at St. Joseph Parish in East Jordan.
Other notable assignments include Reverend Michael D. Class becoming Spiritual Director for Permanent Diaconate Formation Program and Administrator for several parishes; Reverend T. Patrick Maher transitioning to Co-coordinator for Native American Ministry; and Deacon Curtis P. Chambers also named Co-coordinator for Native American Ministry while maintaining his current diaconal duties.
Parish assignments involve several priests moving to new pastoral or parochial vicar roles across various churches within the diocese, such as Father James M. Bearss being assigned to St. Joseph Parish in Onekama while remaining at Divine Mercy Parish in Manistee, and Father Donald R. Geyman moving from St. Paul Parish in Onaway to serve at St. Casimir Parish in Posen.
The Diocese of Gaylord is home to roughly 45,000 Catholics with 75 parishes and 21 Catholic schools; it also supports a Catholic hospital along with multiple day care centers and social service facilities according to diocesan statistics.
The newly announced appointments reflect ongoing transitions within church leadership aimed at supporting parishioners throughout northern Michigan.
